### Age
- **Two rules** → benign = young (most of them)
- Malignant = **>40 years**; age is the single most important clinical fact (Greenspan) · each card names only its **exception**

| Age group (Handbook) | Benign | Malignant |
|---|---|---|
| **0–5** | Eosinophilic granuloma · simple bone cyst | Leukaemia · neuroblastoma metastasis (the "2 early") |
| **6–20** | SBC (simple bone cyst), ABC, eosinophilic granuloma · osteoid osteoma, osteoblastoma · osteochondroma, enchondroma, chondroblastoma, chondromyxoid fibroma · fibrous cortical defect, NOF (non-ossifying fibroma) | Ewing sarcoma · osteosarcoma |
| **21–40** | ABC · giant cell tumour · eosinophilic granuloma · enchondroma | Ewing sarcoma |
| **>40** | Enchondroma | Osteosarcoma (second peak) · chondrosarcoma · fibrosarcoma · MFH (malignant fibrous histiocytoma) · metastasis · myeloma · lymphoma |

- Books → Ewing **5–25** · giant cell tumour **almost never before maturity**
- Osteosarcoma bimodal: second decade + 7th–8th decades, often secondary (OKU Tumors 4; Greenspan; Miller)

### Sex
- **Rule** → **males**, except 3 → ABC, giant cell tumour, fibrous dysplasia (Handbook)
- Books → fibrous dysplasia **equal**; **parosteal osteosarcoma** female (OKU Tumors 4)

### Relative incidence — the rank lines

|---|---|---|
| 1st | Osteochondroma | Metastasis (1st overall) |
| 2nd | Enchondroma · Handbook: non-ossifying fibroma (PITFALL) | Multiple myeloma (1st non-metastatic) |
| 3rd | — | Osteosarcoma (1st primary sarcoma) |
| 4th | — | Chondrosarcoma |
| 5th | — | Ewing sarcoma; 2nd primary malignancy in children (OKU Tumors 4) |

1.04.b:
### Longitudinal location — epiphysis, metaphysis, diaphysis
- **Metaphysis** → **the rule**, most lesions; epiphyseal and diaphyseal lesions are the least common (Prof Abosena)
- **Paired tumours** (rule: they come together in the same places) → metastasis + myeloma · lymphoma + leukaemia · chondrosarcoma + Ewing (Handbook)
- Longitudinal location of tumours in a long bone, slide (Prof Abosena)

| Site | Tumours |
| --- | --- |
| **Epiphysis** | Epiphyseal lesions → 9 Differential |
| **Diaphysis** | **CAR FILM HOME** (below) · books → PITFALL |
| **Metaphysis** | Everything else; includes **chondrosarcoma and enchondroma** |
| **Any site** | Metastasis |

- **CAR FILM HOME** (diaphysis, Handbook) → **C, A, R** chondrosarcoma, adamantinoma, round cell (Ewing)
- **F, I, L, M** fibrous dysplasia, infection, lymphoma, myeloma · **H, O, M, E** histiocytosis (= eosinophilic granuloma), osteoid osteoma, metastases, enchondroma

PITFALL — CAR FILM HOME is half right
- Books → chondrosarcoma, enchondroma **metaphyseal**; metastasis **any** site; Ewing → **diaphysis or metadiaphysis** + pelvis, ribs, scapula (OKU Tumors 4; Miller)
- Say → "diaphysis: Ewing, adamantinoma, fibrous dysplasia, histiocytosis, osteoid osteoma, lymphoma, myeloma, infection"

### Transverse location — central, eccentric, cortical, surface
- Handbook → **eccentric = the rule**; central = 3 → SBC, enchondroma of the hand, fibrous dysplasia
- Greenspan → central = epicentre on the **anatomical axis**, eccentric = away from it; neither is a default
- Central vs eccentric; vertebral body vs posterior elements, diagram (Greenspan)

| Position | Tumours |
| --- | --- |
| **Central** | Simple bone cyst · enchondroma · fibrous dysplasia |
| **Eccentric** | Giant cell tumour · ABC · non-ossifying fibroma · chondromyxoid fibroma |
| **Cortical** | Osteoid osteoma · fibrous cortical defect |
| **Surface** | Benign → osteochondroma, **ecchondroma** (periosteal chondroma) · malignant → parosteal and periosteal osteosarcoma, periosteal chondrosarcoma; all are subtypes |

- **Osteochondroma** → cortex **and** medulla continuous with the host · **parosteal osteosarcoma** → stuck on; CT (computed tomography) or MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) shows marrow invasion · + **myositis ossificans** (Prof Abosena)
- Parosteal osteosarcoma, posterior surface of the distal femur, lateral (Greenspan)

### Special sites — spine, sacrum, pelvis, chest, hand, foot
- The **3 special sites** → spine, sacrum, pelvis; + chest, hand, foot (Handbook)

| Site | Benign | Malignant |
|---|---|---|
| Vertebral body | Haemangioma (jail bar, polka dot) · eosinophilic granuloma (vertebra plana) · giant cell tumour | Metastases, myeloma · lymphoma (ivory vertebra) · osteosarcoma · chondrosarcoma, Ewing |
| Vertebral arch | Osteoid osteoma, osteoblastoma (painful scoliosis) · ABC | Same as body |
| Sacrum | ABC · giant cell tumour | **Chordoma** → most common sacral mass |
| Pelvis | As the spine + chondroblastoma, chondromyxoid fibroma, fibrous dysplasia | **Post-radiation sarcoma** after pelvic radiotherapy |
| Chest | Enchondroma · giant cell tumour | Chondrosarcoma, Ewing · metastases, myeloma · leukaemia, lymphoma |
| Hand | **Enchondroma** commonest, osteochondroma; osteoid osteoma, ABC, giant cell tumour | Rare: chondrosarcoma > osteosarcoma, Ewing (Miller) |
| Foot | Talus: osteoid osteoma · calcaneus: cysts (SBC, ABC, giant cell tumour), cartilage tumours = the "**calcaneus group**" | Calcaneus: chondrosarcoma · Ewing |

- Vertebra → malignant in the **body**, benign in the **posterior elements**, except haemangioma, eosinophilic granuloma, giant cell tumour (Greenspan)
- Real question (Nagah p29) → **Winking owl** → AP spine film, one **pedicle erased** → **metastasis** (body and pedicle destroyed early) · **myeloma** spares the pedicle early (vertebral pedicle sign) (Greenspan p2152, 2192)

1.06.b:
### ① X-ray — why one fixed scheme
- First goal → **benign or malignant** (Prof Abosena) · textbook frame → Enneking's 4 questions: where · lesion → bone · bone → lesion · matrix (Miller); Greenspan adds soft tissue and multiplicity

CLINICAL PEARL — the X-ray is the map (Prof Abosena)
- No diagnosis **without an X-ray** → it is the map and gives a **differential**; pathology decides

| Step | Word | Choices (only these) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Site** | epiphyseal · metaphyseal · diaphyseal |
| 2 | **Centralization** | central · eccentric · cortical · surface |
| 3 | **Behavior** | osteolytic · osteosclerotic · mixed |
| 4 | **Margins** | well-defined · ill-defined (inside: sclerotic rim, moth-eaten, permeative) |
| 5 | **Cortical reaction** | intact · thinning · expansion · destruction (inside: periosteal reaction, soft-tissue mass) |
| 6 | **Special signs** | the named sign or matrix, or "none"; "multiple" if several lesions |
| → | **Verdict** | benign latent · benign active · benign aggressive · malignant |

- **Opening line** (not a step) → view, bone, age if given, physis **open or closed** · **scheme strip** → under every lesion film

MUST-KNOW — the spoken sentence
- "This is a(n) **[view]** X-ray of the **[bone]**, physis **[open / closed]**. There is a **[site]**, **[centralization]**, **[behavior]** lesion with **[margins]** margins."
- "The cortex shows **[cortical reaction]**. **[Special sign]**. So this is a **[verdict]** lesion."
- "In this age and site my differential is **A, B, C**. Next I would ask for **[next step]**."

### Step 4 — Margins
- **Zone of transition** → the **most reliable** sign, lytic lesions only; narrow (drawable with a fine pen) = slow · wide = aggressive, e.g. plasmacytoma, Ewing (Helms; Greenspan)
- Traceable with a finger → **well-defined**, not → **ill-defined** (also the locally aggressive lesion) (Prof Abosena; Handbook)
- Pattern follows growth rate; permeative = round cell tumours (Ewing, lymphoma)

- Borders 1A sharp sclerotic, 1B sharp lytic, 1C indistinct, diagram (Greenspan)
- Geographic, moth-eaten and permeative destruction (Greenspan)

| Lodwick (Miller; Greenspan) | Pattern (I = geographic) | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| IA | Sharp, **sclerotic rim** | Non-ossifying fibroma |
| IB | Sharp, **no rim** | Simple bone cyst |
| IC | **Indistinct** in part | Giant cell tumour |
| II | **Moth-eaten** | Metastasis, myeloma, osteomyelitis |
| III | **Permeative** | Ewing sarcoma |

- Narrow zone (non-ossifying fibroma, simple bone cyst) vs wide zone (plasmacytoma, Ewing) (Greenspan)

- Ill-defined lytic lesion in an adult → "could be anything" → history, MRI, biopsy (Prof Abosena)

- **Moth-eaten** → holes of varying size, normal bone between them; myeloma, metastasis (Prof Abosena)

- **Permeative** → whole medulla, cortical destruction + soft-tissue mass; the pattern of sarcomas (Prof Abosena)

### Step 5 — Cortical reaction
- Handbook → for **lytic** lesions, not osteosclerotic ones; order **1 thinning → 2 expansion → 3 destruction**; destruction tells the grade
- **Expansion** pushes the cortex out · **destruction** → malignant or benign aggressive, but it can **mislead** (infection, eosinophilic granuloma, ABC) → needs other malignant criteria (Helms)

CLINICAL PEARL — expansion comes from the medulla (Prof Abosena)
- Expansion must arise from the **medulla** → a purely cortical lesion does not balloon the bone

- Intact: enchondroma of the distal femur, 55-year-old (Campbell)

| metaphyseal + diaphyseal | central | mixed | well-defined | intact | chondroid calcification | **benign latent** |

- **Curettage** → the last resort; for active lesions it is **simple** curettage · window → curette → fill with bone graft or cement
- Prophylactic fixation → lower limb usually, upper limb by lesion size (Handbook) → 3 Treatment

| Aggressive lesion | Technique | Margin achieved |
|---|---|---|
| **Extended curettage** | High-speed burr + adjuvant → phenol or argon (few mm) · liquid nitrogen (up to 2 cm) | **Marginal** (wall removed by necrosis) |
| **En bloc resection** | Mass + wall + reactive zone + normal cuff; compartment left intact | **Wide** |

- Bone cement advantages → **1** filler + adjuvant by thermal necrosis
- **2** rapid setting (minutes) · **3** recurrence seen earlier than under graft (Handbook)

### Surgical margins — numbered 1–5 (Handbook)
| # | Margin | Removes | Equals |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Intralesional | Lesion from within, walls left | Simple curettage |
| 2 | Marginal | Lesion + walls | Extended curettage |
| 3 | Wide | Lesion + walls + reactive zone + normal cuff | En bloc resection |
| 4 | Radical | Whole compartment | Limb salvage (Handbook) |
| 5 | Amputation | Proximal to the lesion | — |

- Malignant → **3** wide: low grade intracompartmental · **4** radical: low grade extracompartmental or high grade intracompartmental
- **5** amputation: high grade extracompartmental · resection of metastases → stage III (Prof Abosena)

- Amputation is not a 5th margin → resection or amputation × 4 margins = **8 procedures**; limb salvage uses **wide**, not radical (Campbell; Operative Techniques)

- **Local** (surgical) → limb salvage or amputation, aim complete tumour removal · **systemic** → radiotherapy (radiosensitive tumours, metastatic pain), chemotherapy (chemosensitive), hormonal (hormone-responsive) (Handbook)
- **Basic** for every patient → pain control (NSAIDs → morphine → regional blocks), physiotherapy, psychotherapy (Handbook)

|---|---|
| Resection only (low grade) | Chondrosarcoma (chemo- and radio-resistant) · periosteal / low-grade osteosarcoma · adamantinoma |

| Resection + radiotherapy | Chordoma (sacrum) · most soft-tissue sarcomas |
| Resection + chemo + radiotherapy | Ewing sarcoma · fibrosarcoma · rhabdomyosarcoma |
| Chemo + radiotherapy only | Myeloma, leukaemia, lymphoma → no routine surgery |
